notes: CHA2DS2-VASc: CHF 1, HTN 1, age >=75 2, DM 1, stroke/TIA 2, vascular 1, age 65-74 1, female 1. CHADS2: CHF 1, HTN 1, age >75 1, DM 1, stroke/TIA 2.

criteria.span: covers percutaneous LAAC for non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) through Coverage with Evidence Development (CED)

criteria.text: FDA PMA device used for its approved indication
criteria.span: LAAC devices are covered when the device has received Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Premarket Approval (PMA) for that device’s FDA-approved indication
A CHADS2 score ≥ 2 (Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Age > 75, Diabetes, Stroke/transient ischemia attack/thromboembolism) or CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥ 3

criteria.text: Formal shared decision making with an independent non-interventional physician using an evidence-based tool, documented
criteria.span: A formal shared decision making interaction with an independent non-interventional physician using an evidence-based decision tool on oral anticoagulation in patients with NVAF prior to LAAC. Additionally, the shared decision making interaction must be documented in the medical record.

criteria.text: Suitable for short-term warfarin but unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation (second-line only)
criteria.span: A suitability for short-term warfarin but deemed unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation following the conclusion of shared decision making, as LAAC is only covered as a second line therapy to oral anticoagulants

criteria.text: Multidisciplinary team; hospital with established SHD and/or EP program
criteria.span: The procedure must be furnished in a hospital with an established structural heart disease (SHD) and/or electrophysiology (EP) program

criteria.text: Operator: manufacturer training; >= 25 transseptal procedures; continuing >= 25 per 2 years incl. >= 12 LAAC
criteria.span: Has performed ≥ 25 interventional cardiac procedures that involve transeptal puncture through an intact septum

criteria.text: Patient enrolled in a CMS-approved prospective national audited registry
criteria.span: The patient is enrolled in, and the MDT and hospital must participate in, a prospective, national, audited registry
LAAC is non-covered for the treatment of NVAF when not furnished under CED according to the above-noted criteria

cases.note: CHA2DS2-VASc 4 (age>=75 2, female 1, HTN 1); recurrent GI bleeding precludes long-term OAC.
cases.vignette: 78-year-old woman with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and hypertension. She had two hospitalizations for gastrointestinal bleeding on apixaban; her cardiologist and gastroenterologist judge her unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation, though a short course of warfarin after the procedure is acceptable. Before the referral, an independent general internist (not involved in the procedure) held a shared decision-making visit using an evidence-based decision tool on oral anticoagulation, documented in the medical record. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed over 100 transseptal procedures, and in the last 2 years performed 60 transseptal procedures including 30 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
